shared_elements: marks made on a natural stone surface
a figure with limbs/appendages radiating from a central body (quadruped-like or splayed form)
linear incised/pecked outlines rather than painted areas
justification: The only real correspondence is that both are stone surfaces bearing a figural motif with radiating limbs, and both rely on outline rather than colour. Otherwise they are wholly different: A is a single faint, isolated pecked figure on an unbounded, weathered horizontal rock face, whereas B is a deeply carved relief on a shaped upright block with multiple stacked registers of distinct creatures separated by a horizontal patterned band and a row of arcs — no comparable ordering exists in A.
